entities.summary: Czechia is a sovereign nation in Eastern Europe, Europe. Its capital is Prague. Official languages include Czech. Government: Unitary parliamentary republic. Population: approximately 10.9 million. Area: 78,871 km². Comprehensive index for Czechia covering Celtic Boii (Bohemia name), Great Moravia (863 Cyril and Methodius), Přemyslid dynasty, Bohemian kingdom (Holy Roman Empire), Charles IV Golden Age (Prague capital of HRE, Charles University 1348), Jan Hus/Hussite Wars (1419-34, proto-Reformation), Habsburg rule (1526-1918), Defenestration of Prague (1618, triggered Thirty Years' War), Battle of White Mountain 1620, Habsburg re-Catholicisation, 1848 revolution, Czechoslovak independence 1918 (Masaryk), Munich Agreement 1938 (betrayal, 'peace for our time'), Nazi Protectorate, Heydrich assassination 1942, Communist coup 1948, Prague Spring 1968 (Soviet invasion), Charter 77, Velvet Revolution 1989 (Havel), Velvet Divorce 1993 (Slovakia split), EU accession 2004.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Czechia's complex history has had significant regional impact, particularly during the Thirty Years' War and its aftermath, which led to a major realignment of European power dynamics. The Munich Agreement in 1938 also had far-reaching consequences for Czechoslovakia and Europe.
